ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the picture there are five gray puzzle pieces, labeled A, B, C, D, E. The top edge of A is concave inward, and the right edge is also concave inward; the top edge of B protrudes outward, and the right edge is concave inward; the top edge of C protrudes outward, and the right edge also protrudes outward; the top edge of D protrudes outward, and the other visible edges are straight edges; the right edge of E is concave inward, and the other visible edges are straight edges. Reasoning: When four pieces are put together to form a square, the outer boundary of the square must be straight edges, so all curved edges must be paired two by two internally, and concave edges must be paired with convex edges of the same shape. Counting by curved edges: A has 2 concave edges, B has 1 convex edge and 1 concave edge, C has 2 convex edges, D has 1 convex edge, and E has 1 concave edge. If B is not used, then A, C, D, E are used, with a total of 3 concave edges and 3 convex edges, which can be completely paired. If any other piece is not used, the numbers of concave and convex curved edges are unbalanced and cannot all be internally paired. Therefore the unused piece is B.

raw_record.question_text: A square can be made from four of the given pieces. What is the label of the piece that will not be used?

method.method_draft: Use a curved-edge inventory. From the image, classify each labeled piece by the signs of its curved edges: A has two inward/concave curved edges, B has one outward/convex curved edge and one inward/concave curved edge, C has two outward/convex curved edges, D has one outward/convex curved edge, and E has one inward/concave curved edge. From the text, exactly four pieces must form a square, so the chosen pieces cannot leave any curved edge on the outside; every curved edge must be paired internally with a congruent opposite-curvature edge. Check the four-piece sets by omitting one label. Omitting B gives A+C+D+E, with three concave curves and three convex curves, allowing all curved boundaries to be paired. Any set including B instead creates an imbalance or wrong remaining curved boundary. Therefore the unused piece is B.

method.method_draft: Use a constructive assembly starting from the distinctive double-indented piece. From the image, choose A as an anchor because it already has two adjacent straight edges that can become part of the square boundary, while its top and right sides are concave cutouts that must be filled. The broad convex arch of D can be rotated to fit A’s top concavity, and one convex rounded side of C can be fitted into A’s right concavity. After those placements, C’s other convex curved edge leaves one remaining complementary curved contact; the piece with the matching inward curve and mostly straight outer sides is E. The four pieces A, C, D, and E can then be oriented so their remaining straight edges form the outside square. Piece B is not needed because its extra concave side would introduce another inward curved boundary after A’s two hollows have already been filled.
